The display area was clearly not maintained to any acceptable standard, and yet cakes were being sold to unsuspecting customers without a second thought.

This is a basic food safety issue. Flies are carriers of bacteria and disease.. which i ate. The fact that customers are being served food in these conditions is not just disgusting.. it is a health hazard. Had a child eaten that cake, or had this happened to someone less composed, the consequences could have been far worse.

I strongly urge the management to take immediate action not just a surface level cleanup, but a thorough review of hygiene protocols, food storage practices, and display standards. This is not acceptable for any food establishment, let alone one selling celebration cakes.

Shame on you for letting it get to this point. Do better.

After that, they said they will not take my order in future and even told staff not to accept my order. This feels like personal targeting/discrimination, which is completely unacceptable.

Overall, this place seriously needs improvement in:

✅ Staff behaviour & professionalism
✅ Clear responsibility between hostel and café setup
✅ Cleanliness and hygiene (table clearing)
✅ Fixed and transparent pricing/menu

featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re someone who loves the charm of classic Mumbai street food culture, this roadside Irani café tea stall is an experience you should definitely try. It may not be a polished or modern setup, but it has an old-school authenticity that many regulars find irresistible.
The highlight here is the iconic Irani chai—rich, aromatic, mildly sweet, and brewed with the perfect balance that true Irani tea lovers cherish. It has that signature creamy finish and comforting warmth that instantly makes you slow down and savour the moment. Pairing it with their delicious bread maska is an absolute must. The bread is soft, lightly toasted, and generously buttered, making it a simple yet memorable treat. Together, the chai and bread maska form a classic combination that captures the heritage of Mumbai’s Irani cafés beautifully.
However, the environment around the stall is something to be aware of. Since it’s located in a highly crowded, traffic-heavy area, the atmosphere can feel a bit chaotic. Parking is mostly on the roadside and not very convenient, so expect a bit of hassle if you’re driving. The surroundings can be slightly dusty, with plenty of small kiosks around, adding to the typical Mumbai roadside buzz.
Despite these challenges, the quality of the food stands out every single time. The flavours are genuine, comforting, and absolutely worth the visit. If you’re looking for an authentic, no-frills BKC snack experience, this Irani tea stall is highly recommended.

featured_reviews.name: Rishi Goswami
featured_reviews.review_text:
Je vous présente: Le Bazar des Rêves Brisés.

We arrived, hoping for a sanctuary: a haven of pristine contemplation where one might sip an artisanal coffee in the esteemed, silent company of literary legends—of Ginsberg's, of Plath's, of Keats. The aspiration, stamped into the glossy lease of this mall locale, was clearly to be a temple to the printed word.

The immediate reality, however, was a profound and shattering dissonance. The ambiance they desired to project was intellectual refuge; the reality they achieved was that of a fish market near a crowded railway station during a particularly raucous local festival. The air hummed not with quiet discovery, but with the high, frantic anxiety of total disorganization.

This establishment suffers from a chronic and debilitating lack of internal coherence. There is no evidence of management or any guiding organization—only the haphazard stacking of commerce upon chaos. It becomes apparent that the staff are not curating an experience but merely enduring a shift, their movements suggesting a perpetual, bewildered search for something misplaced, perhaps their own dignity.

The inventory, that sacred heart of any bookstore, is where the illusion completely dissolves. One searches, with quiet despair, for anything beyond "The Usual Suspects"—those run-of-the-mill, safe editions destined only for airports and bedside tables. The rare, the classic, the demanding titles are conspicuously absent, rendering the store’s literary pretensions hollow. Furthermore, the casual confirmation received on the phone regarding the availability of specific, requested books proved to be a lie, told perhaps out of habit or sheer, indifferent fantasy.

But the moment of ultimate, symbolic betrayal arrived not with a book, but with a beverage. In the middle of this poorly managed chaos, I spotted a small, tantalizing stack of Coca-Cola cans. Upon asking for one, I was delivered the definitive, breathtaking punchline: “No, that is for the owner. You must go down to the mall food court and get your own.”

To keep a product on display while simultaneously reserving it for the owner, denying the patron even the simplest act of commerce, is not merely bad service—it is a philosophical statement. It is a brilliant, miniature demonstration of utter lack of respect for the customer, revealing the entire venture as a mere show, designed for self-gratification rather than public engagement.

Coupled with a singularly uninspired coffee, and the unavoidable, crushing anonymity of its big mall location, this bookstore fails on every conceptual level. Go only if you seek an overwhelming sense of disappointment and a potent reminder that the purest acts of literature should perhaps remain strictly transactional and conducted at a distance. Welcome to the chaos.

The ambiance is beautiful — cozy, minimal, and perfect for chit-chat, reading, or working on your laptop. They have both indoor and outdoor seating, making it a great spot to enjoy a cup of coffee and unwind.

Since it’s strawberry season and the Christmas vibe is kicking in, this café is the perfect place to indulge in some festive flavours! 🍓🎄

🌟 What we tried:

featured_reviews.name: Soumitra Sinha
featured_reviews.review_text:
Six of us walked into Grounded Cafe this morning after a nice Sunday morning long drive. Pretty hungry of course. Very chilled out ambience. A real cafe atmosphere. The food orders were varied --- from a full English breakfast, Eggs Florentine to Pancakes and Crepe; coffees and an Orange flavoured hot chocolate.  Great tasting fresh food served with a smile. The hash browns as a side needs a special mention....just the right crisp with a yummy inside. We were so happily full that a single portion of Nutella Tiramisu was ordered for us to share. Don't miss this desert as the cup and cover are made of Nutella.
Now folks, that is what I call an amazing Sunday breakfast.
Great place. Great food. Great ambience.😃

featured_reviews.name: Shamim Akhter
featured_reviews.review_text:
A great cafe located very close to Band Stand, yet tucked away in a corner away from the noise and crowd.

Great place to grab a quick bite and superb coffee, though the first time I went there my friend had to ask to remake her chocolate drink as she could hardly taste any chocolate in it.

The croissants and French fries are amazing.

The receptionist staff are extremely attentive.

The outdoor seating is a great place to be during sunset and sea-breeze, though the wind can be a bit too strong if you are trying to light a cigarette.

The friendly neighborhood cat that saunters around is an added attraction.

The café also allows you to bring in your own pets.

featured_reviews.name: Anchal Bakshi
featured_reviews.review_text: If you’re strolling around Bandra Bandstand, Grounded is a cozy, aesthetic café perfect for a quick escape. The vibe is lively with both outdoor and indoor seating, though the music can be slightly loud at times. Their coconut latte and mocha frappe are refreshing highlights, while the nachos and avocado toast make for great, satisfying bites. The staff is warm and polite, but the serious is very slow but definitely a lovely spot to hang out and unwind.

featured_reviews.name: Dinesh Katke
featured_reviews.review_text: If you’re wandering around Bandstand in Bandra and looking for a cozy spot to refuel, Grounded is a fantastic choice. The overall ambience is incredibly pleasant, making it a perfect escape from the hustle and bustle of the promenade. The highlight of my visit was easily the Callebaut Hot Chocolate with whipped cream. It was absolutely delicious rich, velvety, and honestly one of the best hot chocolates I’ve ever had. To balance the indulgence, I tried the Healthy Chicken Ragi Wrap. It’s rare to find something that feels both nutritious and genuinely tasty, but this wrap nailed it. The staff also deserves a special shoutout; they were super polite, kind, and made the experience feel very welcoming. The only minor drawback was the music volume. It was a little loud for my taste, which made conversation a bit tricky at times. However, that’s a negligible part of an otherwise awesome experience. Between the quality of the food and the kindness of the team, I’ll definitely be back.

featured_reviews.name: Nalini
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had brunch here for the first time after hearing about it from colleagues. I ordered the Truffle cheddar scrambled eggs and a black tea .
The scrambled eggs were delicious and served with a salad and sourdough bread . Excellent combination. The tea was Twinings so a clear focus on quality.
Here is where I was disappointed ..the music at first was way too loud to finish my work, let alone think but a lady called Jhanvi very sweetly noticed and lowered the volume.
Also in attendance were a couple of flies (unnecessary desi touch ) and my eggs were served in a chipped plate.

However, on the positive side, Ebrahim and Imam were warm and friendly , served my food , asked how it tasted  and kindly returned my sunglasses I left behind . It didn’t feel forced .

Afterwards I spoke to Jhanvi ,the sweet smiley lady who rescued me from going deaf and turns out she is in charge of Marketing. She was most responsive to my feedback .

I wish this beautiful located Cafe the best of luck and hope they do well enough to lower the prices a tad . For my eggs and tea I paid Rs 736, of which Rs 96 was service charge + taxes. Left a rather small cash tip as I paid a 10% service charge .

Speaking of which , they lost electricity just when it came to swiping my credit card so I paid in cash.
All in all a cute pricey place with a menu that’s trendy .
